# Ogg reader fixture

`vorbis-silence.ogg` contains 0.1 seconds of original, generated silence
(48,000 Hz, mono Vorbis in an Ogg container). It contains no third-party audio.
The reader-selection regression embeds it so tests do not require FFmpeg's
optional `libvorbis` encoder. The separate Opus audit still invokes FFmpeg.

Generated using FFmpeg 9.0.1:

```bash
ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=48000:cl=mono -t 0.1 \
    -c:a libvorbis -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact -map_metadata -1 \
    -f ogg packages/opus/tests/fixtures/vorbis-silence.ogg
```

SHA-256: `e9473eb3cc486ddf8b9cbf75b2c2f3f5d59c6729fdc4515ea774148a65557c25`

Encoder/library versions may change the generated bytes. Check codec, channel
count, rate, and duration with `ffprobe` before replacing the fixture.
